newsitem.title: UK: UK tax experts seek simpler regime from budget.
newsitem.headline: UK tax experts seek simpler regime from budget.

text.p: Representatives of leading British tax experts on Thursday called on Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown to simplify the tax regime and lessen the burden on people with low incomes.
The Chartered Institute of Taxation said Britain's tax system was too complex and flawed by too many short-term and expedient changes.
"Let's get rid of short-term expediency which has made our tax system a disgrace," said John Andrews, president of the Institute in a statement.
"This is not the time for a mass of hastily thought through tax changes. We need a statement of long-term economic policies and a description of the tax vision in support of those policies."
He said the Institute was campaigning on behalf of those who cannot afford to pay for help in managing their tax affairs.

"Although many of the Institute's 10,000 members make their livings as professional taxation advisers we also believe strongly that people on low incomes should not have to pay fees to complete their tax returns or have to spend time seeking help from their tax office," Andrews said.
He said the new 'self-assessment' taxation system was causing real problems for many people on low incomes who are not accustomed to employing accountants.
The Institute called for a national insurance to be integrated with income tax, and to conduct a wide-ranging consultation on tax law.
